text:
alex_c: Hey — heads up, seeing a weird packaging/CI failure on macOS arm for the python SDK installs from our internal index. Nightly sample app installs the package and then fails at import with a dlopen symbol error. Logs:
```
ImportError: dlopen(/private/var/.../redwood_sdk/_native.cpython-310-darwin.so, 0x0002): symbol not found: _some_native_init
  Referenced from: /private/var/.../_native.cpython-310-darwin.so
  Expected in: flat namespace
``` 
But `pip show redwood-sdk` reports a wheel file with tag `py3-none-any.whl` (so pip thinks it is pure). We definitely ship a compiled extension for the native KV cache shim, so that mismatch is surprising.

riley: oh interesting. Did CI upload an sdist only and our artifact index auto-converted to a wheel? Some indexes will do that and mark it universal if the conversion step didn't set root_is_pure=false.

sam_k: yep that rings true — our release job has historically uploaded the sdist and relied on the index to build wheels. If the index builds a wheel but the builder doesn't detect compiled extensions, it might mark it as "any". That would cause pip to grab an "any" wheel on mac that actually contains a compiled .so for x86_64 only (or built on the wrong runner).

ci-bot: nightly/sample-app-macos-arm failed: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/3421 — failure looks like the import error alex pasted. (automated)

alex_c: Workaround for devs: `pip install --no-binary redwood-sdk` or build from source. But that's a terrible onboarding experience for new users on Apple Silicon.

riley: long-term fix: publish platform-specific wheels in the release pipeline (build on each target or use cibuildwheel) and upload those artifacts instead of raw sdists. Also ensure `bdist_wheel` config sets `root_is_pure = False` when compiled modules exist so wheel tag is platform-specific.

sam_k: Agreed. Also check our pyproject.toml / setuptools config: if extension modules are defined but the build step runs on the x86 runners that produce x86 wheels then mac-arm users will still get incompatible binaries if the index serves the first matching wheel. We should produce manylinux/aarch64 or universal2 mac wheels as appropriate.

alex_c: There's also a subtle poetry thing — when we build with poetry building an sdist, the dependency lock metadata can cause pip resolver to prefer the wheel artifact with the wrong tag. Noted.

riley: I'll open a GH issue with the release pipeline checklist and a proposal to switch to cibuildwheel and explicit wheel uploads. Will add migration notes for support and a temporary doc snippet for onboarding: "If you hit ImportError on Apple Silicon, install from source or use --no-binary until fixed." :thumbsup:

sam_k: assign to me for the pipeline changes. I'll also add a CI job to sanity-check wheel tags on publish (fail if py3-none-any contains .so files).

alex_c: Thanks — that should stop a lot of confusion for customers. Can we also add a small unit in the sample app quickstart that runs an import on mac-arm matrix? Saves us chasing onboarding bugs.

riley: will add to the ticket. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
